title: Residence order - can a wife claim a right to the shared household
p1:
Can a wife be asked to leave a house just because it is not in her name?

Many people assume property ownership decides who can stay. But the law has a different answer in certain situations.
p2: A residence order under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act can protect a woman's right to live in the shared household. The surprising part? The house does not always have to be owned by the wife or even jointly owned by her.
p3:
The idea behind this protection is not to transfer ownership, but to prevent a woman from being unfairly removed from a home where she has lived in a domestic relationship. Courts consider factors such as the nature of the relationship, the circumstances of residence, and the facts of each case.

The practical takeaway: a right to reside and a right to own property are two different legal concepts.

Knowing this difference can prevent many misunderstandings during family disputes.
conclusion: Did you know that a person can have a legal right to reside in a home without having ownership rights? Share your thoughts on whether residence rights should be better understood.
